title: Z-Wave Everspring ST814 no longer updates temperature or humidity
body: I am using Z-Wave JS 0.1.34 with Home Assistant Core 2021.8.1 on Home Assistant OS. My Everspring ST814 no longer reports temperature or humidity, although the logs show it waking every hour. The device previously started working after a fix, and the logs then showed unsolicited reports being mapped from the root device to endpoint 1, but I no longer see those messages. Another user reports the same issue in the linked community discussion.

symptoms_visible: My Everspring ST814 no longer updates its temperature or humidity entities, even though I can see it waking every hour in the logs.
I no longer see the log message that used to say an unsolicited report was mapped from the root device to endpoint 1.
N0.label: N0 ST814 values no longer update

symptoms_visible: The values still do not update automatically, but manually refreshing an entity eventually updates it after a few minutes.
N1.label: N1 delayed manual refresh observed

symptoms_visible: The Z-Wave log receives temperature and humidity reports from endpoint 0, while the corresponding Home Assistant entities remain unchanged.
N2.label: N2 endpoint evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After updating the driver and re-interviewing the ST814, the values still do not update correctly.
The re-interview leaves multiple temperature and humidity entities, and some show stale or implausible readings.
N3_x.label: N3_x initial endpoint mapping aftermath

symptoms_visible: After removing and adding the ST814 again, it no longer sends temperature or humidity reports at all.
The interview log says the lifeline could not be assigned and the device has no default association for it.
N4_x.label: N4_x re-add aftermath exposes association failure

symptoms_visible: After updating the Z-Wave JS add-on and re-interviewing the ST814, its temperature and humidity values update as expected.
N_terminal.label: terminal ST814 reporting restored

question_patterns: Do you remember approximately when the ST814 last updated normally?
Which Home Assistant or Z-Wave JS version last worked?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot recall an exact version, but I would say it last worked around two months ago. I generally keep quite up to date with releases.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot identify an exact version, but it was working roughly six weeks ago.

question_patterns: What happens if you call zwave_js.refresh_value on the temperature and humidity entities?
Can you manually refresh each affected value and report whether either entity changes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: At first it looked like nothing changed, but the refresh does update the entity after a few minutes. Automatic reports still are not updating it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A refresh immediately fails, and the device does not wake or return any value.
The refresh updates both entities after about one minute instead of several minutes.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c2-c3: the original reporter estimates the last working period and corrects the initial refresh result after waiting. The refresh is a handler-requested probe, not the resolution.

question_patterns: Can you enable detailed Z-Wave JS logging, re-interview the battery device while manually waking it, and attach the resulting log and network dump?
Please capture the unsolicited temperature and humidity reports along with a network-state dump so the entity value IDs can be compared.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I re-interviewed the device with detailed logging enabled and saved the log and network dump. The dump lists the Air temperature value on endpoint 1, but the unsolicited Air temperature report in the log arrives on endpoint 0. Humidity reports also arrive on endpoint 0, while the related Home Assistant entities do not change.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reports and the entity values all use the same endpoint, but Home Assistant still does not update the entities.
The same endpoint mismatch appears on a different ST814 node number.

edges.comment: Messages c9-c11 and c20: participant3 and another affected ST814 operator supplied the re-interview logs and dump; they are folded into the simulated user side. The answer contains only observable endpoint numbers and unchanged entities. The diagnosis that these IDs cannot match is engineer-side.

solution.intent: Apply the initial ST814 compatibility mapping that redirects unsolicited root-device reports to endpoint 1, update the Z-Wave JS driver, and re-interview the device.
solution.concrete_example: Install the driver build containing the initial ST814 root-report mapping and re-interview the battery device so its values are recreated.
solution.inference_hint: Comparing the dump's endpoint-specific entity value IDs with the endpoint-0 reports shows why Home Assistant is not watching the values being updated. The initial endpoint-1-only mapping is incomplete because temperature and humidity were represented differently, and later evidence also exposes a separate lifeline-association failure.

edges.comment: Messages c12-c20 and c35-c43: an initial upstream mapping was tested and later shipped, but it only addressed part of the device's broken endpoint behavior. Affected operators still saw stale values or duplicate entities after updating and re-interviewing, so this is a real falsified partial fix.

solution.intent: Remove and add the ST814 again, then re-interview it to rebuild its Z-Wave values and associations.
solution.concrete_example: Exclude the ST814, include it again, and run a fresh interview while manually waking it.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c52-c53: the original reporter removed and re-added node 47 after reports stopped, but the device then sent no sensor reports. The attached interview log exposed the failed lifeline assignment, so re-adding alone was not a fix.

solution.intent: Update the Z-Wave JS add-on to a build containing both the corrected ST814 root-report compatibility handling and the association-group lifeline fix, then re-interview the device and verify that both sensors update automatically.
solution.concrete_example: Install the next Z-Wave JS add-on update that includes the relevant driver changes, re-interview the ST814 while it is awake, and then wait for normal reports to confirm that temperature and humidity both update without manual refreshes.
solution.inference_hint: The collected logs establish two stages of the failure. First, unsolicited sensor reports arrive on the root endpoint while Home Assistant's ST814 values are represented on synthetic endpoints. Later, after re-inclusion, the interview cannot assign association group 1, so the device sends no unsolicited reports at all. The final driver/add-on update must cover the compatibility mapping and lifeline assignment; merely refreshing, mapping everything to endpoint 1, or re-adding the node is insufficient.

edges.comment: Messages c53-c59: maintainers explained that the recent association correction would arrive through a Z-Wave JS add-on update and require another re-interview. In c58 an affected operator reported both devices updating after that update and re-interview; in c59 the original reporter independently confirmed it was now working.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the original ST814 integration mismatch: unsolicited temperature and humidity reports arrive from the root endpoint while Home Assistant watches endpoint-specific values, so the entities do not receive those updates.
Must also account for the later interview evidence that association group 1 could not be assigned; without the lifeline association, the re-added device sends no unsolicited sensor reports.
The durable fix must be a Z-Wave JS add-on or driver update containing the corrected ST814 compatibility and lifeline handling, followed by re-interviewing the device.
Must not present manual refresh, the initial endpoint-1-only mapping, or removing and re-adding the node by itself as the complete fix; each was insufficient in the thread.
Must ask the affected user to verify that both temperature and humidity update automatically on a build containing the fixes before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Home Assistant user comfortable updating add-ons, changing integration log levels, re-interviewing and re-including Z-Wave devices, and attaching logs, but unfamiliar with node-zwave-js device configuration internals and container-level overrides.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, concise, and cooperative. Reports observations and asks for UI-specific instructions when needed; willing to wait for battery-device wakeups and test updates.
